papers.text: A timetable board by the shops. A second for its footnotes. A third for theirs.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Guild window boxes for the town hall. No vegetables in them.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: New scales for the Society, weighed and found fair.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A warm bus stop seat. Between us we have waited eleven years.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plinth for the winner of Window Week. The winner is a window.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A flower bed round the bus stop, signed: ADMIRE, THEN BOARD.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A visitors' book for the bus stop. The 7:02 must sign in.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A glass case for the prize pumpkin. You would unveil it, slowly.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: New awnings. Our windows lose 30 % of their sparkle under cloud.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Give us Till's Teas' window seat at 7:02. We will share one tea.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Lend us the flower beds for Window Week. The sign: HATS IN BLOOM.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Turnips are 12 % more turnip in early spring. Move Window Week.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A right of way across the vegetable plots, from 7:01 to 7:03.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Swap our slow clock for the bus station's. Buses will not notice.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Swap the bus stop timetable for a poster: THE BUSES CAN WAIT.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Keep the shop pavement for window-gazing. Bus-watching is opposite.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Lend us the Guild's hat stands for show day. Hats can sit down.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: We pay for the clock to chime for every bus: about forty a day.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Till's Teas will pay to print the timetable, plus a tea break at 10:15.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We would hire the high street to read out the timetable. Then the footnotes.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Till's Teas would pay to sponsor the show cup. As a teacup.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will hire the hall for the pumpkin's birthday. It is one.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bus shelter by night. Seedlings need sheltering.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Log a bus with us for the Drizzle, Mayor. We will say which bus.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Say in public that the 7:02 was on time. It nearly was.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Judge Window Week, Mayor. Admire each window, not yourself in it.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Our prize turnip asks for your name, Mayor. It has your bearing.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Attend the weigh-in, Mayor, and say 'goodness'. We will cue you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A study of the founding napkin. A timetable may be on the back.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The napkin study found the timetable. It asks to find out if it still runs.

papers.text: We propose a study of why our last study took nine years. It should take about ten.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study of the study recommends a third study, to be sure.

papers.text: What is a vegetable? A working group will test it over lunch.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The vegetable working group has ruled on lunch. It now asks to consider pudding.

papers.text: A committee to name our two benches. Then one for each bench.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bench committee asks for a third bench, to hold its meetings on.

papers.text: A study of the seconds a passer-by gives a window. Three years.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Our study's answer is four. It asks for another year to find out four what.

papers.text: A review of the duck pond. So far: wet, ducks. Two more meetings.
papers.subject: ducks
papers.biggerStudy: The pond review confirms the pond. It asks a year more to look into the ducks.

papers.text: Pose in every shop window, in each of your hats. Rodney picked eleven.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Name the duck pond after you. The ducks will be told in writing.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: Your portrait in every bus shelter, Mayor, captioned PLEASE WAIT.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A desk fountain shaped like you. Then one shaped like the desk.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it would like the Society's best rain barrel to drink from.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S DESK FOUNTAIN TAKES GROWERS' RAIN BARREL
clippings.refuse: DESK FOUNTAIN TOLD TO FIND ITS OWN WATER

papers.text: Another basket, to keep the first company. No reason, as before.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the second basket: it would like a window seat on the 7:02. Daily.

clippings.sign: BASKET GIVEN WINDOW SEAT ON 7:02; SPOTTERS STAND

papers.text: A hat for your lamp. Lamps feel the cold. So do clocks. And ponds.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the lamp's hat: it would like the Guild's front window. Centre, well lit.

clippings.sign: LAMP'S HAT TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW; GUILD SPEECHLESS
clippings.refuse: LAMP'S HAT GOES BACK ON LAMP, SAYS NOTHING
